subject.title: Feature: Inject context window % into system prompt runtime section

question: Should OpenClaw expose passive context-window usage in every system-prompt Runtime line, and should the contract be percentage-only, token/window, or omitted when the snapshot is stale or unknown?
rationale: The implementation path is clear, but this changes model-visible prompt bytes on volatile per-turn data and may affect prompt-cache behavior, so code inspection cannot choose the product contract.

options.title: Approve bounded Runtime field
options.body: Add `context=NN%` from fresh session total/context tokens, omit it when unknown or stale, keep it below the stable cache boundary, and leave raw details to status/session tools.

options.title: Keep explicit status/tool surfaces
options.body: Decline passive prompt injection and keep context usage on `/status`, `/usage`, `/context`, `session_status`, or future runtime tools only.

options.title: Fold into runtime self-context
options.body: Track this under the broader runtime self-context design, but require that design to handle dynamic context pressure before closing this narrower issue.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Runtime field
recommendation.body: Add `context=NN%` from fresh session total/context tokens, omit it when unknown or stale, keep it below the stable cache boundary, and leave raw details to status/session tools.

likelyOwner.reason: The core prompt/runtime metadata history and the product-contract nature of the decision point to the system-prompt owner signal rather than a code-only fix owner.
